# Reviewer verdict: BLOCK

PR #264, round 1 of 2. Exact head: f808581187bf33c0513a637304264e9e4029ecb3.

## R264-001 (P2): refusal recovery instructions assume the default highlight

Location: `crates/harnesses/src/trust.rs:89-94`, with the fixed instructions at lines 57 and 66-67, consumed by `crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:2011-2024`.

`safe_answer()` ignores the prompt's observed `highlighted` row. Unlike `next_key()`, it always returns the default-row instructions. The no-flag refusal therefore gives the wrong recovery action on a supported, committed screen: `copilot-1.0.114-folder-trust-second-row.txt` highlights `2. Yes, and remember this folder for future sessions`, but the refusal says to press Enter and describes that action as trusting this session only. Following it persists folder trust instead. Claude's committed yes-row fixture is similarly told Down then Enter although its trust row is already selected.

This affects F215's primary no-flag recovery path, not speculative hardening. Have the refusal tell the person to select the named trust row before Enter, or derive navigation from the observed highlight; do not describe an unconditional Enter as session-only trust. When the highlight is unavailable, name the target row rather than inventing a safe key. Extend the existing nondefault/no-highlight fixture assertions to cover the refusal guidance, not just automatic `next_key()`.

## Other requested checks

- The five live prompt fixtures cover the stated tall/short/second-row cases. The classifier is not a general guarantee against quoted text: Claude accepts matching option rows anywhere in the screen, even without its workspace heading. A multiline menu quotation can therefore match. This is a known matching limitation from source inspection, not a separately reproduced normal-startup blocker.
- The opt-in path uses the observed highlight: Claude's No row produces Down, the trust row produces Enter, and no highlight refuses. It reclassifies each capture, so the inspected control flow stops sending keys when the prompt disappears. Menu keys are a closed enum; the one-second settle interval bounds key sends.
- The refusal uses the existing F211 failure helper. It preserves the launched seat/pane/spawn identifiers, writes `spawn.failed`, and calls `watch.failed`, not `answered`; the existing two-fact handoff handles later or concurrent binding.
- F216 goes directly to `/v1/close` by seat ID. Caller resolution, contradictory-attribution refusal, self/recorded-parent ownership and designated-prime dead-orphan authority remain in the daemon. No PA branch was added.
- `kill_pane` follows the existing pane-ownership predicate, is validated as `%N` in the TS decoder, and is suppressed on a held close. The extension kills only that returned pane. The pane-identity checks are one-directional safety interlocks (brakes): removing them permits more kills; they are not retention policy.
- Removing the boot-roster close and its otherwise-unused reducers leaves no callers of `requestClose` or `applyTerminalObservation`. Durable close truth now comes from the daemon's tombstone and role-ending path.
- Existing nonblocking teardown-reporting limit: the concrete TS `TmuxAdapter.killPane` swallows execution failures and returns success, so the new `killed`/`killFailed` reporting cannot detect those failures. This root predates the PR; the former close also relied on that adapter result. Performance reviewer pij-united-dragonfly independently raised it.

## Cost

The existing registration-wait loop sleeps 50 ms between iterations (at most about 20 iterations/s per active spawn wait, plus work time). The change reuses its single visible-screen capture and adds only in-process row classification; no new healthy-seat loop or capture launch. `--trust-folder` adds at most one recorded `tmux.send-keys` launch/s per opted-in active wait, and only while a matching prompt remains. No fleet measurements or builds were performed by this correctness review seat; live cost receipts belong to the separate performance verdict.
